seat_audit:
## OK  Thiên Xu Tông (thien_xu; leans Metal/Earth)
Seat: Thiên Xu Tông (id 5, great_seat, region 14, high mountain), density 2.11
Seat qi: Metal 29%, Earth 33%

ground.name: Trích Tinh Phong
ground.gloss: Peak Where One Picks the Stars
ground.note: Lý Bạch: thủ khả trích tinh thần (one could pluck the stars by hand); 4.7 km, the roof of the heartland

ground.name: Tinh Tủy Mạch
ground.note: A wild vein high in Dao Quang Lĩnh, near Trích Tinh Phong, 4 tiles from Băng Tâm's border.

ground.name: Vạn Trùng Hạp
ground.note: Lý Bạch: khinh chu dĩ quá vạn trùng sơn (the light boat has passed ten thousand mountains)

ground.name: Bạch Ngân Khoáng
ground.note: Silver below the cinnabar mountain of Đan Sơn Mạch.

ground.name: Phá Quân Môn
ground.note: The mountain fort of the vassal that rebelled against Thiên Xu.

ground.name: Can Tương Khoáng
ground.note: Can Tương, the swordsmith of legend; Phất Y Cốc's swords are forged from its ore.

ground.name: Tinh Lạc Hồ
ground.note: A high lake, 1.2 km up, that holds the Dipper at night; beside Củng Tinh Quán

ground.name: Thiên Ngoại Khoáng
ground.gloss: Mine of the Iron from Beyond the Sky
ground.note: Thối Tinh Môn forges star iron, and says this is where it comes from.

events.text_en: Chung Hoài Cực, at 80, founds Thiên Xu Tông under the stars of the Northern Dipper; the ground around his seat grows rich as the sect gathers, and becomes the Bắc Thần Phúc Địa.
Under Thiên Xu Tông's protection the traders' crossing grows into Thạch Kiều Thành, the first city of the heart.
Củng Tinh Quán's star-readers find that the high lake Tinh Lạc Hồ holds the Dipper at night as clearly as the sky.
Iron from a fallen star is dug at Vẫn Tinh; Củng Tinh Quán keeps the mine.
The star-readers of Củng Tinh Quán finish the Tuyền Cơ Nghi, an armillary that follows the Northern Dipper through the year.
A market of weight and measure opens beside Thiên Xu Tông; it is called Thiên Quyền Thị, and its scales are the fairest on the continent.
Thiên Xu Tông takes the ore mountains of Ngọc Hành Sơn under its protection, and wins the miners with fair weights, not swords.
Thiên Xu's assayers weigh the miners' ore on open scales in the square of Song Kiều; no miner of Ngọc Hành has rebelled since.
Now that Thiên Xu's assayers weigh ore in public at Song Kiều, the miners stop coming to the bosses' gate, and Thiết Môn Bảo is left.
Thiên Xu Tông extends its protection north over Dao Quang Lĩnh; its borders will not change again.
Thiên Xu's first watchmen climb Trích Tinh Phong and report that one could pluck the stars by hand.
Thiên Xu Tông founds Tinh Hán Thành, its port on the inland sea, on the reef of the old sea-serpent's bones.
Kỳ Tùng Ẩn and Chung Hoài Cực meet at Thạch Kiều Thành and drink for three days; the Pine and the Pivot keep the peace for two centuries.
Black iron is found deep under the mountain at Huyền Thiết; it is so heavy that a cart carries only one ingot.
Thiên Xu Tông founds Khai Dương Thành on the northern road.
A jade-green brook below the ridges gives Bích Khê Trấn its name and its trade in river jade.
Cinnabar is found in the red badlands; Thiên Xu's alchemists open Thần Sa Khoáng.
Smiths who quench star iron in the mountain river found Thối Tinh Môn under Thiên Xu.
Thối Tinh Môn claims the Mine of the Iron from Beyond the Sky and says its ore fell with the stars.
Thiên Xu disciples begin to leave for Cửu Thiều Cung after hearing its music; Chung Hoài Cực calls it a theft of minds and marches south against Lạc Thiều Âm.

In the War of the Nine Shao, Thiên Xu Tông under its founder Chung Hoài Cực, accusing the sound arts of its southern neighbour Cửu Thiều Cung of bending the minds of its disciples, destroys it; its last head Lạc Thiều Âm falls in the palace's last stand. The grounds lie empty.
A year after the palace falls, mourners still climb the hills to sing its songs over the graves; Thiên Xu does not stop them.
Deer gather each spring in the high meadow of Lộc Uyển; Thiên Xu forbids hunting there.
Pearl oysters in the shallows of the inland sea give Châu Bạng Thôn its name and Tinh Hán Thành its pearl trade.
Sulphur crusts at Lưu Hoàng make the badlands smell of eggs for twenty li; Thiên Xu mines them for fire powders.
Silver is found below the cinnabar slopes at Bạch Ngân; Thiên Xu's coin is struck from it.
Thiên Xu finds the Star Marrow vein high near Trích Tinh Phong and posts a guard that has never been withdrawn.
The Tuyền Cơ Nghi shows the Dipper's handle turned toward the heart; Củng Tinh Quán warns of war, and no one listens.
Tùng Đào Cung and Lạc Hà Tông march together on the heart of the continent; Kỳ Tùng Ẩn breaks the peace of the three days.
Thiên Xu Tông breaks Thiết Tỏa Quan; the thousand-fathom chain sinks to the river bed.
The iron chain breaks below a bare peak on the river road; the peak is called Đoạn Liên Phong from that day.
The War of the Pivot ends: Thiên Xu Tông has beaten Tùng Đào and Lạc Hà together, and takes no land.
On the day the Compact is signed, every bell in Thạch Kiều Thành rings without being struck.

In Thạch Kiều Thành, Chung Hoài Cực sets the North Star Compact before the seven sects and stamps it with the Bắc Thần Ấn: land changes hands only by a fall, a gift, an oath or a war the Pivot licenses by writ, and Thiên Xu Tông will enforce it.
Thiên Xu Tông founds Thanh Bách Thành on its northern road.
With the Compact set, the garrison of Tây Quan Bảo stands down, and its stones are carried off to build Thanh Khoa.
Unpaid since the Compact, the last soldier-farmers of Đồn Điền Trại leave their fields for Thạch Kiều.
A swordsman who brushes his sleeve and leaves after every deed founds Phất Y Cốc, and digs the ore of Can Tương for its swords.
Phượng Minh Cung asks the Pivot for a writ against Xích Thành Môn, which has burned eleven villages; the first writ of the Compact is granted.
Light glints so brightly on the mountain lakes at Ba Quang that travellers think the village is on fire.
Scented wood from the groves of Mộc Hương Thôn is burned in the hall of the Pivot.
Thối Tinh Môn forges the halberd Trầm Sa Kích from star iron for a young officer of Thiên Xu, Quý Trường Kích.
The last master of Bạch Lộc Quán, the abbey that asked Thiên Xu to ban hunting in the deer meadow, dies without a disciple; the halls are left to the deer.
Boats in the gorge of Vạn Trùng Hạp pass ten thousand mountains in a day; the river is the fastest road to the sea.
The Pivot's judgement divides the Petal Shore, the bay to Lạc Hà and the forest to Thính Vũ; Lạc Hà renames the bay city Tử Điện Thành, for its armoury.
The grain road moves to Song Kiều, and the miners' granary stockade of Tích Lương Trại is left.
The head of Khuy Thiên Các goes blind, and its star-readers join their old rivals at Củng Tinh Quán, carrying their charts with them.
Tùng Đào takes the Cold Ford coast and Hàn Tân Thành; Chung Hoài Cực, Kỳ Tùng Ẩn's old drinking friend, lets it stand, and the Compact's first crack shows.
Cranes return to the marshes on the same day every year; the village where they land is named Hạc Quy, and Cửu Cao Phái rides the first of them.
The water mills at Thủy Đối grind the wheat of Thanh Mạch for all of Tinh Hán Thành.
Crane riders tame the first cranes of the nine marshes in Dao Quang Lĩnh and found Cửu Cao Phái; their cry is heard in the sky.
In a dry summer fire starts in the pitch yards of Chi Hương Trấn and burns the town and the forest around it; no one rebuilds.
A landslide buries the toll stockade of Hạp Khẩu Trại, and the ore road is moved to the other bank.
Hạ Lang Tinh founds Phá Quân Môn in the mountains of Dao Quang Lĩnh as a vassal of Thiên Xu, named for the Dipper's seventh star, the Army-Breaker.
The Pivot imposes a truce on the Desert Road; the caravans pass again, and the border stays where it was.
Phá Quân Môn's disciples begin to drill at night on Phụ Tinh Phong, under the faint companion star.
Chung Hoài Cực dies at 720; Đỗ Tinh Hà, then 200, becomes the second head of Thiên Xu Tông.
The night the founder dies, a boy is born in Thạch Kiều Thành under the fifth star of the Dipper; he is named Doãn Ngọc Hành.
The last abbot of Thanh Đăng Tự dies with no disciple, and the lamp the monks kept for travellers goes out.
Đỗ Tinh Hà calls the Pirate Purge; Phượng Minh's and Lạc Hà's fleets sail under the Pivot's writ, and Thạch Cơ Thành rises around their stone jetty.
The Purge ends at Thôn Hải Môn: Ô Kình Hải dies on his islet and his sabre Kình Nha is lost in the burning hold.
Đỗ Tinh Hà names Quý Trường Kích war marshal of Thiên Xu, and gives him the Thiết Mã banner and its tally.
The Tuyền Cơ Nghi goes dark for a whole night; Củng Tinh Quán's star-readers burn incense and wait for war.

War breaks out on the border plain where three sects' lands meet: Thiên Xu Tông, under its war marshal Quý Trường Kích, against Lạc Hà Tông and Thính Vũ Lâu, whose founders Nhan Cô Vụ and Phó Tiêu Tương take the field.
With Thôn Hải destroyed in the Purge, Thiên Xu stands down the sea patrol fort of Tuần Hải Bảo.
Quý Trường Kích raises the old ramparts of Cố Lũy on the edge of the plain and holds them for five years.

At Chiết Kích Nguyên the war ends in one day. Quý Trường Kích falls and ten thousand die with him; the plain is poisoned with miasma, and the Vạn Cốt Trủng rises over the dead. His lieutenant Lôi Vô Danh escapes and is never seen in the sect again.
Vô Định Thành burns in the battle on the plain, and the miasma takes what is left; its dead are still dreamed of in the river towns.
Quý Trường Kích is laid under the Vạn Cốt Trủng with his halberd Trầm Sa Kích; its iron has not worn away.
The three sects sign a truce and leave the poisoned plain empty between their lands.
At the truce the North Star Compact is sworn again; Lạc Hà and Thính Vũ set their seals beside the Bắc Thần Ấn.
No one has come to relieve Lang Yên Trại since the battle on Chiết Kích Nguyên, and at the truce the signal outpost is abandoned.
After the truce the Pivot stands down its beacon line, and Phong Toại Bảo is left with its fire basket cold.
No riders came back from the battle to claim their remounts; the herds of Lão Mã Bảo are sold and the fort is left.
After the truce the Pivot stands down Nam Vọng Bảo, its border watch above Kinh Lôi Mạch.
With the North Star Compact sworn again at the truce, the Tower pulls the walls of Vọng Xu Bảo down to knee height as a sign of good faith.
Hạ Lang Tinh leads Phá Quân Môn against its lord, to win by war the land the Compact forbids.
In the rebellion, Cửu Cao's crane riders carry Thiên Xu's messages over Phá Quân's fort.
Two years after its head left on a journey and never returned, the sabre fighters of Hoành Đao Môn have scattered.
Thiên Xu destroys Phá Quân Môn; Đỗ Tinh Hà takes Hạ Lang Tinh's spear, and Cửu Cao Phái receives the rebels' holdings.
When the rebellion is crushed, the garrison of Phá Quân Môn's Vọng Tinh Bảo surrenders without a fight; the fort is burned and left.
The rebel gate of Phá Quân Môn falls, and Thiên Xu abandons Vi Thành Trại, the siege camp it raised three years before; soldiers' names stay scratched on its stones.
Phá Quân Môn's mining town of Hắc Thạch Trấn passes to Cửu Cao Phái, but its people have already fled to Cự Môn, and none come back.
Fewer and fewer take up the hard life, and the last desert cells of Khổ Tu Viện stand empty.
After three centuries of digging out their halls, the last disciples of Minh Sa Các give the pavilion to the dunes and go to Thạch Kiều.
Khai Dương Thành's gate is rebuilt to face the morning star; travellers say the city wakes before the sun.
A boy of Thụ Âm Thôn follows his goat into the miasma and walks out three days later, grey-haired and calm.
The Ôn clan builds the twin bridges of Song Kiều over the river road, and keeps the tolls.
Thúy Vi Tông, holding the Pivot's writ, marches to take back the Cold Ford.
Talisman makers who paint the Dipper's stars found Họa Tinh Đường and swear to Thiên Xu; their talismans will not run in the rain.
An earthquake splits the cistern of the caravan city Lục Hợp Thành and dries its springs; its people move to Thạch Kiều.
The well of Khô Tỉnh Trấn fails in the drought, and the caravan town's people leave for the river.
Thiên Xu clears Hắc Phong Trại, where rogue cultivators (tán tu) have robbed the ore trains for sixty years.
Đỗ Tinh Hà arbitrates the Long Lake War: the lake stays Tùng Đào's, and Băng Tâm may fish its northern shore.
A storm tide drives over the quay of Cựu Tân Trấn and takes half the town; the rest move inland to the lakes of Ba Quang.
A star falls near Thanh Bách Thành; the fragment is sold to Thối Tinh Môn for three years of the city's taxes.
Vệ Văn Cơ is born in Tinh Hán Thành and draws formations in the harbour sand before he can talk.
Assayers and refiners of spirit ore found Chân Kim Các beside Song Kiều's open scales, sworn to Thiên Xu.
The harbour of Ngân Thuyền Bảo has silted up; the silver goes overland to Song Kiều, and the fort is left.
An avalanche buries Thủ Bi Trại, which guarded a boundary stele of the Compact; the stele is moved lower.
Ung Hạc Minh is born in Hạc Quy Thôn; that year the cranes stay a month longer.
The warding pillars are raised over the vent, and the Pivot withdraws the garrison that has watched it from Thủ Hỏa Bảo.
In the Thunder Vein War, Phượng Minh's raiders reach the upper ferry at Thượng Độ before the Pivot's envoys stop them.
The Pivot ends the Thunder Vein War: Thính Vũ keeps the vein, and the south remembers.
Thạch Kiều Thành's stone bridge, the oldest thing in the heart, is widened for the first time; the old stones are kept in the Pivot's hall.
Cát Lưu Quang becomes head of Thối Tinh Môn and forges a blade from the star that fell near Thanh Bách.
Pill refiners using the cinnabar of the red badlands found Hoa Cái Đường under Thiên Xu; their pills are weighed at Thiên Quyền Thị like everything else.
A Vạn Hác student plays so well under the pines that Thiên Xu's envoy forgets his message.

Thiên Xu Tông calls a hunt under the North Star Compact for the ma đạo master Mặc Huyết Sinh; with Tùng Đào Cung and Băng Tâm Các at its side, Đỗ Tinh Hà, Thôi Khinh Hồng and Sở Ngọc Hồ kill him in his cave abode. His last disciple Triệu Huyết Y, then 150, escapes.
The pilgrims' road up Trích Tinh Phong is cut into the rock in a thousand steps.
Doãn Hi Hòa is born in Thạch Kiều Thành at sunrise; Doãn Ngọc Hành takes her as his disciple when she is five.
Tư Không Hạc Niên duels Thang Vô Tạ of Phất Y Cốc on Cùng Mục Phong for three days; neither wins, and he leaves without a sect.
After the duel on Cùng Mục Phong, Thang Vô Tạ will not speak of it; Phất Y Cốc's disciples climb the peak to see the sword marks.
Lễ Tuyền Phái's spirit wine is served at the Pivot's table for the first time; Thiên Xu orders a hundred jars a year.
Đỗ Tinh Hà steps down after 390 years; his disciple Doãn Ngọc Hành becomes head of Thiên Xu Tông and keeper of the Bắc Thần Ấn.
Doãn Ngọc Hành brings Thiên Xu Tông into the war on Phượng Minh's side, to enforce the Compact.
Thính Vũ Lâu is beaten at Đan Sơn Mạch and withdraws; Mạnh Dạ Vũ swears the Pivot will answer for it.
Seven years after Đan Sơn Mạch, Thính Vũ Lâu has rebuilt its strength twice over; the Pivot's envoys count its disciples and do not like the number.
The blue haze on Thanh Ải Phong lifts for a day for the first time in memory; a temple is seen on the summit, and by evening it is gone.
Băng Tâm Các claims Tinh Tủy Mạch before the Pivot; the claim is rejected, and Sở Ngọc Hồ withdraws in silence.
After Băng Tâm's petition, Thiên Xu doubles the guard on Tinh Tủy Mạch; Cửu Cao's cranes circle it day and night.
With its claim to the vein rejected and Thiên Xu's guard doubled, Băng Tâm withdraws the watchers of Khuy Tinh Bảo and bars the doors, so as not to look like war.
Ung Hạc Minh tames a crane king that will let no one else ride it.

wars.name: War of the Nine Shao
wars.outcome: Cửu Thiều Cung destroyed for arts that bent the minds of others' disciples; Thiên Xu takes none of its land. Thiên Xu's first judgement.

wars.name: War of the Pivot
wars.outcome: Tùng Đào and Lạc Hà try to take the heart of the continent, the crossroads of every route. Thiên Xu beats both, takes no land, and imposes the North Star Compact in 510.

wars.name: The Pirate Purge
wars.outcome: Called and led by Thiên Xu with Phượng Minh's and Lạc Hà's fleets; the ma đạo pirates of Thôn Hải Môn are destroyed.

wars.name: War of Broken Halberds
wars.outcome: Lạc Hà and Thính Vũ break the Compact together. The war ends in one day at Chiết Kích Nguyên in 803; Thiên Xu holds but loses its marshal and ten thousand dead; the 805 truce renews the Compact and leaves the poisoned plain empty.

wars.name: Phá Quân Rebellion
wars.outcome: A Thiên Xu vassal that wanted conquest rises against its lord and is destroyed; Cửu Cao Phái receives its holdings.

wars.name: Cinnabar Vein War
wars.outcome: Thính Vũ attacks Phượng Minh's Đan Sơn Mạch; Thiên Xu steps in on Phượng Minh's side and Thính Vũ is beaten.

cast.name: Doãn Ngọc Hành
cast.gloss: Ngọc Hành is the fifth star of the Northern Dipper, the one that weighs

build.note: The Pivot's cautious keeper of the Compact: fights from inside his own arrays behind stone wardens, and never steps out of them

cast.name: Chung Hoài Cực
cast.role: Founder of Thiên Xu Tông (year 120, at 80)

cast.name: Quý Trường Kích
cast.role: Thiên Xu Tông's war marshal in the war on the border plain; held the ramparts of Cố Lũy
cast.cause: fell at Chiết Kích Nguyên (age 243); buried in the Barrow of Ten Thousand Bones

cast.name: Lôi Vô Danh
cast.role: Quý Trường Kích's lieutenant, who survived the war on the plain and hid; owner of the cave abode in slot A-3 (Thiên Tuyền Nguyên)

cast.name: Đỗ Tinh Hà
cast.role: First elder of Thiên Xu Tông (age 640); its second head, 760-1150, who stepped down for his disciple, the head Doãn Ngọc Hành

build.note: Four centuries of the Pivot's wars: a spearman of the Phá Quân spear who patiently waits for one called, killing blow

cast.name: Doãn Hi Hòa
cast.role: The head's disciple and presumed heir, age 70

build.note: The presumed heir: her master's canon at its first layers and an ambitious edge she has not yet learned to sheathe

legendary_items.story: Stamped the North Star Compact in 510; every writ of war since bears its mark.
legendary_items.name: Bắc Thần Ấn

legendary_items.story: The rebel vassal's spear, taken when Phá Quân Môn was destroyed in 874.
legendary_items.name: Phá Quân Thương

legendary_items.story: Whoever holds it commands the army that waits in the realm.
legendary_items.name: Thiết Mã Phù

legendary_items.story: The marshal's banner, carried off by Lôi Vô Danh. With its tally it raises the army.
legendary_items.name: Thiết Mã Kỳ
